text_fidelity_a:
94 Piece First Aid Kit Packed with First Aid and Survival Essential by Sirius Survival A good first aid kit is a good thing to keep in the car when traveling and I selected this kit to keep in one of the vehicles because all of us are road warriors these days. Of course, the hope is that it is never needed, but when one is needed it's an invaluable resource. This is an interesting kit, and it has some pluses and minuses.

This is a small kit that fits nicely under a seat, in a seat pocket, or in a center console. Finding a place for it in a car or truck should be no issue at all.

There's a lot going on in this kit. It has a lot of the typical first aid items - bandages, gauze, cotton swabs, anticeptic wipes, and even a foil emergency blanket. There's some really odd things in here too - a flint, a compass, a whistle and a multi-tool are the stand-outs. This is not a typical first-aid kit but is also a basic survival kit.

The multi-tool is the standout in the whole kit and is worth the cost of the whole kit. It seems to be made fairly well, it is heavier than some of the cheaper ones I have seen and used and it has the basic tools you'd expect - pliers, a knife, screwdriver, etc. It includes a set of bits as well.

The compass is relatively cheap but it does work.

The remainder of the components in this kit are farily nondescript. All will work in an emergency capacity.

As a first aid kit this isn't so bad. However, this thing tries to be a survival kit as well, and on that basis there's an important omission - there's no flashlight in this kit. Even a small $5 flashlight would make this kit more complete and capable.

This certainly isn't a bad kit, but it tries to be two different things and as a survival kit it comes up a little short. This will serve well for a traveling family and in a pinch it will make a decent emergency kit, but I would not rely on it as a sole source.
text_fidelity_b: 94 Piece First Aid Kit Packed with First Aid and Survival Essential by Sirius Survival

text_fidelity_a: V12 Fitness & Health Smartwatch with Activity Tracker 24/7 Heart Rate Monitor Blood Oxygen Spo2 Scientific Sleep Monitor IP68 Waterproof Exercise Sports Pedometer Watch for Running Walking (Grey) I got this watch because it needs to be charged every day or every other day. I also got this because it states it is waterproof. That is not true. The IP in IP68 stands for Ingress Protection. The 6 stands for prevents dust entering the insides. The 8 means suitable for immersing underwater for an indefinite period at any depth. But the manufacture determines the depth and length of time. So, it is not truly waterproof. In fact, the included instructions indicate you should not soak the device, do not wear to swim, dive or take hot showers. You can wash your hands and take a cold shower. The general rule for IP68, is that it prevents dust from getting in and you can be in the water for up to 30 minutes for 1.5 meters. And never submerge in salt water.

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman Approved Mount Bike Rack I have a great Swagman bike carrier from before (I believe it is an XTC) that I always liked, but wanted this one for the option of carrying heavier bikes. Even better is that this on has integrated locking arms, the one thing that was missing from my XTC (I think I got a version that was just one generation too old).

Anyway, this one seems to have it all with the only tradeoff being that it will only work with a 2" receiver, so if you have a regular car that you might want to haul with one day, you're out of luck.

It does everything right: ratcheting rails with integrated locks, the type of compression tighteners (tightened by hand) that won't leave a screw mark on your carrier, and a threaded hitch pin to reduce wobble. It does sort of take some time to figure out how to get any pair of bikes set up together without interfering with each other, but once you get it figured out the first time, you're set. If you use multiple different pairs of bikes, you'll have to try to remember from one set to the next (of you'll be lucky and both will be able to use the same setup. For me, once I had my pair on there in the right manner, I haven't had a problem since then.

Very happy with the quality - and certainly the rigidity - of this bike carrier.

text_fidelity_a:
Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce I really hate being the first and only 4 star review but here goes..

I got mine from RawReform, whom I dearly love, and was pleased to get it very quickly and loved all the goodies that came with it.
I HIGHLY recommend that you watch the DVD on the immune system that came with it - very interesting and well done informationally. Mine also came with a book, "Rebounding For Better Health" which I also recommend reading. This book enlightened me and I learned so much from just reading this very simple book!
I'm also glad I did as I learned the importance of 'bouncing' before you 'jump'; and what great benefit the 'health bounce' has for your body!

I completely concur with the other reviewers on the quality of the Needak and would never advise buying BELOW this quality standard. I have not tried folding it yet, so I cannot comment on the ease of doing so. (Unfolding was easy.)

(I had an entire review written and almost completed when my computer fritzed, so I'm trying to remember all the points I had previously written.)

There were a few reviews in particular that cinched the deal and 'sold' me on getting mine. I had recently been troubled with hip problems that a Chiropractor had made MUCH worse (not ALL chiros, just this one) and was getting concerned about my hip/knee pain. My normal forms of exercise were also making it worse and so I wanted to see how rebounding would help.
Let me tell you that with just a couple minutes here and a couple minutes there of doing the 'health bounce' alone has made remarkable differences in my hip/knee pain (almost gone); noticeable improvements in the 'elimination' area; and giving me deeper, restful sleep and less irritability. AND, I've even noticed a slimmer tummy!
Now, how can this be??!!! I'm only doing a COUPLE minutes here and there!
Yet, the book and the DVD will explain how this form of body movement affects your body at the deepest level - the CELLULAR level!
With that information - with those results - how is it that people aren't STAMPEDING and buying these things faster than Amazon can sell their KINDLES!!??
I think it's just a matter of time, and they will.
I realized I had been in the 'dark' too long to not have known the incredible benefits that rebounding/bouncing does for your health, but not any more!

Now..why the four stars instead of five? Well, four is still good. Even three is good. Because, although it says Soft Bounce, it was harder than I imagined. At this time, bouncing with both feet is uncomfortable for ME. My legs throb and ache. So, I've gotten around that by doing a sort of dance 'Twist'; some Jumping Jack type moves and hops and that seems to do the trick. Am I just more out of shape than I thought? Will it eventually improve? I don't know. I'll let you know.
I can't help but wish that I were able to COMPARE my rebounders bounce/feel with other rebounders of EQUAL or GREATER value in order to see if another would've been more comfortable for me, but I'll not ever have that opportunity to do so; and this was my price range and I am content with it and would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier This thing is totally awesome. I was actually unaware that such fishing rod carriers existed. And of course, I barely had to browse other models to tell Thule would be a top contender.

Construction is fantastic. Rigid metal tubes and hardened plastic casing make "vault" an acceptable term for this.

One thing I didn't realize was that with this one (unlike the tackle fishing carriers), the length is not adjustable. The tubing is the same diameter for the entire length, so the two 5' sections connect in the middle with a compression connector tightened by hex screws. Because of this, you probably need to lock both parts of this to your rooftop rack, which leads to me locking...

...Locking this up is probably the weak point for me. This is unfortunate, because I always want better locking on any device, but this one isn't even as good as I might expect out of Thule. For one thing, it doesn't have the "one key" feature that Thule started using at some point (but you had to special order your device with your key type already if you wanted to go with that, so maybe consumers were too lazy to do it and the company gave up on it...not sure). Worse, though - and a real concern - is that this and my tackle vault use the same key, which leads me to wonder if I am able to open up and steal from any Thule rodvault I see out there in the wild? (Of course, I'd like to believe that anyone with enough money to buy a rodvault would be unlikely to steal fishing stuff from another person, but who knows...). Also, you need padlocks to lock the vault to the rack, which isn't that big of a deal, but I've seen other equipment with integrated locks that used the same key as the rest of the equipment, so it could be better.

This is big and heavy. More so than I expected. That adds some sense of value to it, but it also has me rethinking my storage place, especially considering its 10' permanent length unless I want to disassemble it with every use.

I'm also curious if this would hold some deep sea poles. I think so, but don't have any yet to try for myself.

In conclusion, it's hard to not be impressed with this thing, and yet I see some areas for improvement, mostly in the locking scheme. It is hard not to give this a full five stars simply because of its excellent sturdiness and bringing a whole new excellent way to transport large, expensive poles with even a small car, and without having to worry about them at all, for the most part.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier

Peltor Soundtrap/Tactical 6-S Electronic Headset, Neckband Style, NRR 19dB My wife and I have owned this model for about five years with no issues from workmanship. These are good reliable active earmuffs and we like the fact we can hear each other well when speaking but it actively blocks loud sounds. However if you are getting these for shooting primarily at indoor shooting ranges you might want to consider something with more than 18dBa protection. We've found that we end up adding foam ear plugs when there are others in an indoor range shooting high caliber firearms, plus if you wear safety glasses (which you should be doing) it can lesson the ability of the cups to form around your ear.
Lastly the changing of batteries is not great. You basically have to take a small flat screwdriver to pry up the ear cups. Over the years my screw driver has slipped and I've poked holes in the actual ear cup foam! And you need to make 100% sure the cover snaps back in completely after swapping batteries else you will be in for a loud surprise when using those the next time, meaning if not sealed properly it will not block as much sound.
I've found that I've put these aside except when I need to hear someone speaking while wearing protecton. Instead I've gone with a simple foam in ear version similar to this model for shooting: https://www.amazon.com/Hamilton-Buhl-NoiseOff-26dB-Black/dp/B01MYUO3ET
text_fidelity_b: Peltor Soundtrap/Tactical 6-S Electronic Headset, Neckband Style, NRR 19dB

Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board Cornhole is a fun game that brings back memories of “Toss-Across” for me. I never had heard of, or played, cornhole until it was introduced to me at a social gathering relatively recently. I have wanted my own set for taking to family functions and picnics with friends, and this set is well suited for these situations.

I will start with this: I received the tailgate version which is a little smaller than the regulation size set. The difference is that the boards are a foot shorter. That’s ok, but it does mean that my set is not suitable for true tournament play and instead is geared for casual competition. Both sized sets are available here; make sure you get the size you want. While it may be a little smaller, it has two distinct advantages. First, it is lighter so it is easier to carry. Second, because it is smaller it is more compact and can be stored (and transported) more easily too.

This set is made to be portable. Most sets I have seen have been made of plywood and have fixed legs. To move them is awkward and often unwieldy. This set instead has an aluminum frame and lightweight boards so the weight is substantially reduced. The legs fold under, allowing the set to lay flat. This makes it a lot easier to pack the set for travel and to store it away when not in use. An important detail – when the legs are down they lock in place with a metal bracket so the board will not collapse.

The set comes with 8 bean bags, 4 blue and 4 red. These are regulation size and are interchangeable with other sets.

So far my family is very pleased with this set. It is made very well, it is compact and portable, and because this set (in my case) is the tailgate version it is lighter and easier to store when not in use. This is an easy product to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board

text_fidelity_a:
GINTRON Fitness Tracker, Activity Tracker with Blood Pressure Heart Rate Monitor Watch, IP67 Wateproof Sleep Tracker Pedometer Step Tracker Calories Counter Watch for Men Women Teens The manufacturer of this device, which is a fitness tracker shaped like a watch with an associated phone app, claims that it offers the following functions: Bluetooth pairing with the phone app, pedometer, heart rate monitoring, blood pressure monitoring, blood oxygen saturation monitoring, controlling music playing on the phone, monitoring exercise goals, sleep tracking, alarm clock, alerting the user to an incoming phone call or SMS text on one’s cell phone.

PROS

1. The outward appearance of the watch is attractive and functional.

2. The watch is lightweight.

3. The pedometer function is useful.

CONS

1. This device comes with a pathetically insufficient manual. This is a major failure. The manufacturer has attempted to put the limited instructions it provides in eight different languages, printed on a single, double-sided, 7x14-inch piece of paper. This includes instructions not just for the watch itself, but also for the phone app that goes with it. For a user to have a chance of figuring out how to use a complex device like this, it is absolutely essential to have access to an adequate manual. Here is just one of many different examples of how atrocious this manual is: There is a single sentence devoted to the music-control function of the watch: "Switch to the music interface to control the mobile phone music table to play, pause and switch songs." The above confusing sentence has no relevance to understanding how to utilize that function, and there is nothing else in the manual about it.

2. The manufacturer states in the manual that this device cannot be used to give you medical information. If so, then why include functions for providing readings of blood pressure, heart rate, and blood oxygen saturation? All of these readings are absolutely medical information, which doctors’ offices routinely measure on all of their patients.

3. With a lot of tedious experimentation, it might be possible to figure out some of the non-health-related functions offered by this device, such as: controlling music on the phone from the watch, setting an alarm, alerting the user to an incoming phone call or SMS text on one’s cell phone. But my question is, what is the point of those functions when, in order for the watch to access them on one’s cell phone via wireless connection, the user would have to be carrying their phone with them? And if the user is carrying their phone anyway, why not just look at the phone itself for controlling these functions? Why bother to have this complicated watch as an intermediary? It makes no sense.
text_fidelity_b: GINTRON Fitness Tracker, Activity Tracker with Blood Pressure Heart Rate Monitor Watch, IP67 Wateproof Sleep Tracker Pedometer Step Tracker Calories Counter Watch for Men Women Teens

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite Keeper 785 Integrated Bicycle Lock Chain Bike Lock, 33.5-Inch, Red Bicycle locks come in lots of different strength/security levels. This is not a great lock. If you look at Kryptonite's web site, this is their cheapest and lightest weight chain lock. They give it a 5 out 10 rating. The Kryptonite Evolution chain lock gets an 8/10 rating and the Kryptonite New York chain gets a 10/10 rating. Those are both heavier and more expensive locks.

This Keeper lock is probably OK for lower risk situations, like daytime use at school or for short trips to the supermarket or a restaurant. It's also OK in rurals areas etc where there aren't a lot of bike thieves. This lock is much better than a cable lock (which mostly can be cut with small wire cutters), but a thief can probably still cut this with a heavy duty bolt cutter.

In the big city, this lock is far from sufficient as your only lock. Get a heavy duty lock as your primary lock (for your frame and rear wheel) and maybe use this as a secondary lock (for your front wheel).
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite Keeper 785 Integrated Bicycle Lock Chain Bike Lock, 33.5-Inch, Red

Amazon Essentials Women's Studio Sculpt Mid-Rise Capri Yoga Legging I usually size up a little for yoga/fitness pants, since I am a large medium/small large. These are sized as expected, but if you're like I am (between sizes), go up for more comfort, or go down for more compression and tummy support--either should work fine, depending on your preferences.

The fabric is opaque, so that's excellent--no see through stuff, so you can do your poses without worrying about that.

The problem I have is this: the band on the waist is placed and fitted in such a way to almost emphasize a belly roll. I'm meaty but athletic, and my tummy is relatively flat because my skin is still tight and I have a lot of muscle underneath my extra padding (I love food, and exercise is a way to let me eat, not to try and be skinny. I just don't care about that at all, really!). Most pants don't result in a bulge at my lower abdomen. None of them, really, unless the waistband is high and too tight. With these, it almost creates a pocket, where the top and bottom of the band are both quite tight compared to the middle un-seamed section with two layers of fabric. Those two layers are not really doing their job, so you end up with this loose middle section right at the crest of the lower belly. What's that do? It creates a small doughnut of skin. Not a look I am going for, and probably not one you are either. These pants are weird--I own like a million leggings. It's basically what I wear all the time. These are the only ones that really do this. I dunno...not the best design, and the sculpting is NOT what you want!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Essentials Women's Studio Sculpt Mid-Rise Capri Yoga Legging

KastKing Sharky Spinning Fishing Reel Ultra Light Weight Freshwater Professional Open Face Reel With Features Found Only On Top Quality Penn Shimano Daiwa and Okuma Spinning Fishing Reels I love to go freshwater fishing and this weekend I approached the lake with a brand new weapon - a KastKing Sharky 6000 spinning reel. This is a serious reel that made a good day of fishing even better.

I will start by saying that even though it is approximately the same weight as my primary reel - a KastKing Orcas 4000 - it is significantly larger. I spooled on over 200 yards of 10-lb. test fluorocarbon line and it still had room for more line on it. I put it on an 8' limber rod and headed out to a productive spot.

I am very fussy about my reels and I expect them to meet several criteria. I want a good cast range, a smooth cast, smooth retrieve, quiet operation and a zero-reverse clutch. There has to be enough clearance between my knuckles and the bail to keep it from rapping me on the knuckles when I retrieve. And finally, the drag has to work and be easy to set. The Sharky met every one of these requirements.

I learned fast (and the hard way) that the reel is more than accommodating when it comes to casting and more than once I sent my lures into the trees instead of to the edge of the bank when I was unable to hit the bank with other reels on identical rods. This required a little adjustment on my part but it meant I did not have to work as hard and it also meant I could hit farther targets when I wanted to. So, when I fish from the bank I have a better range into whatever water I am fishing.

The retrieve is glassy smooth and very fast too. Not once did I have a problem with snarled line on the retrieve when I had near-zero load which is a problem on some reels. I like that I could bring in the line very quickly when needed (like for grabbing the net to assist another fisherman). The reel is quiet when spinning - not silent, but quiet.

When the ant-reverse clutch is engaged there is no reverse at all. To me this is a sign that the reel is quality made and is assembled well. I really, really dislike reels that do not have a zero-reverse clutch, and even worse is a reel that has one but it still has just a little play in it. The Sharky’s zero-reverse is solid and works exactly like it’s supposed to work - absolutely zero reverse.

The bail spins an inch or so away from my knuckles but never once has it hit my hand when spinning.

The drag set is uniform and smooth and does not really get harder to turn until close to the end of the tightening range.

In appearance this is a very attractive reel, black and red with a little bit of chrome. It is surprisingly lightweight for the size. I have bigger hands than average so a reel this size that doesn’t add much more weight is very welcome.

The reel helped me land a good variety of fish including largemouth bass, crappie and a near-citation yellow perch. The most exciting catch was a largemouth bass which was not huge but not small either and provided the best test of the reel under stress, and the reel brought this fish to the boat easily without incident. Even under the load of a fighting bass the reel was just as smooth in operation as when retrieving a test plug.

I am very, very pleased with the Sharky 6000 and will be using it again in the same lake in a few weeks. It has not let me down even once and it works very well. If you want a larger reel that works great and does not add a lot of weight to your gear, take a very close look at this reel.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

When it arrived it was a lot smaller than I expected (2.6 x 1.8 x approximately 5 inches). However, when I inserted the required AA batteries and hit the power button I was very surprised by the amount of illumination it puts out. Even a brightly lit room this adds even more light. Do note that the AA batteries are not included.

One of the reasons this works so well is the reflector that makes maximum use of the light put out by the LED arrangement. I did test it at night as well and it worked perfectly on my enclosed patio. I could actually read by it in an otherwise dark room. If there is a shortcoming, it's the actual level of brightness. You can ruin your night vision by looking directly into it. It's best used as an overhead. Plus since the part that houses the reflector and LED is clear all around, it's not directional and can affect night vision of anyone on a space like a camping tent unless you take care in where you hang or place it.

I am not sure how waterproof this lantern is. The battery compartment is in the bottom and there appears to be no seal to keep out any water (and I did not test it). Hanging or off the floor it should not be a problem, but if you are looking for an emergency light that must withstand the elements this is probably not what you want. If you intend to use it as depicted - an overhead in a tent or hanging camping lantern - this is a handy light source. For me I have mine in a drawer for occasional in home use for then we lose power (a too common event in central Florida). It's small enough to stay out of the way, but functional enough to provide a nice amount of light when needed.

To build muscle, you need to lift weights or otherwise add weight to your body in some way. Dumbbells are a good way to accomplish this and a good option for those who want to lift their weight is this set of Adjustable Dumbbells, from Vivitory.

I’ve used many dumbbells in my day, but this is the first time I have ever had a set that was adjustable. You adjust the weight by removing or adding steel bars and by doing this, you can reduce the weight down to about 5.5 pounds each or even less if you leave off the caps. The maximum weight for each dumbbell is about 18 pounds with all the rods in place. This is enough weight range to make these dumbbells using for many strength- building routines.

Removing and adding the weights to these dumbbells takes time, so don’t go into this thinking it’s going to be quick and simple. It will take effort, but it’s still simple enough that most people wont mind. The reason it takes some effort is because you also have to make sure the pads are in place, otherwise the steel rods will move around while you do your workout.

These dumbbells are easy to grip and they look better than traditional dumbbells, which feature free weights. The colorful appearance is cool, not that this means much for working out, but it does look nicer, less industrial/rugged than the traditional style. And the bars hold in place well- you don’t need to worry that they will fall out while you use the dumbbells.

Strength building is important to those who exercise. A good set of dumbbells can make strength building easier and If you’re the type who doesn’t want to mess with free weights, you might consider this dumbbell set from Vivitory. It’s a good set for those who want a single set of dumbbells for their workout routine.

I'm a fast middle distance runner (ie 10k up to half marathon) so I typically don't need a ton of gels/water like those running full marathon and longer distances. I prefer to run without a belt/vest if possible.. but this is the best hydration solution I've tried in terms of being minimal, breathable and not impeding my running form very much.

As other reviewers have mentioned, it does run a bit snug and can be difficult to pull on if you are in between the size ranges but I believe this is intended to keep the belt secure from bouncing around. I have a 31 inch waist and 36 inch hips, Camelbak lists the S/M as being for 28-32 waist and 30-35 for the M/L size so I am between sizes but I think the S/M was the right call because the larger size would probably bounce around too much.

My one complaint with this belt is that I wish there were more pockets with secure closure. There is one zippered pocket and all the rest of the pockets just have elastic at the top to prevent items from spilling out (and a drawsting/cinch for the rear water flask pocket). The key pocket does have a clip to prevent your keys from falling out which is nice but I wish the side pockets had a snap closure or something because I have had items fly out when I was trail running and jumping down ledges.

Overall, this is a great belt and I would recommend it for those looking for a minimalist solution.. the included flask only holds 17 oz so its not a ton of water but if you hate running with heavy hydration gear then this is a great solution.

text_fidelity_a:
G4Free Sport Outdoor Waist Pack Tactical Sling Bag Hiking Fanny Pack Fishing Tackles What a GREAT pack! When I agreed to write an honest review in return for a tan pack, I was thinking this would be a slight improvement over your run-of-the-mill fanny packs. OMG, this thing is brilliantly designed! It's got so many nooks and crannies and mesh pockets and loops and cinches and straps, all very thoughtfully laid out, that it makes you want to go somewhere just so you can load it up and wear it. It would be a great pack for an emergency bug-out bag. Now I know what I'll keep my emergency mylar blankets, waterproof matches, and dynamo flashlight in so if we have another bad winter like this past year they'll be totally handy.

The way this pack is designed, I can see myself using it as my only purse and keeping the major essentials in it at all times. The included shoulder strap would make this very doable, but I like it that the strap can be removed if you want to carry it by the top handle and/ or wear it as a fanny pack. The Big Costco Buy would definitely be easier if I wore this at my waist instead of trying to carrying a purse. The way it's designed, the zippers in the top compartment, which is the logical place to put money and credit cards and a cell phone, face toward your body when you are wearing this as a fanny pack, which adds a level of security whether you're in a store or on the trail. It is so flexible in terms of what you can do with it that I'm just knocked out. I really do love it!

The largest compartment is not quite wide enough for my ASUS MeMO Pad FHD 10 (10.1") tablet, not if I want to zip it around all the way, but it holds my Kindle Paperwhite in a Versa leather-look case and only misses being able to hold the tablet by a bit. It may be that when the stiffness of the fabric and zippers loosens up with use, as it will, the tablet will fit fine and the zipper will close all the way.

This pack looks pretty indestructible, too, for a fabric pack. It is very well sewn and fortified, and if I had not been given this pack for review, if I had seen one up close and personal when kicking around town, I would have wanted one and asked where the person got it. Don't even hesitate.
text_fidelity_b: G4Free Sport Outdoor Waist Pack Tactical Sling Bag Hiking Fanny Pack Fishing Tackles

text_fidelity_a: FoldyLock Clipster Folding Bike Lock - Award Winning Wearable Compact Bicycle Lock - Ultra Sleek Lightweight Smart Bike Security Accessory with Key Set for Bikes E Bikes and Scooters - 75 cm The Clipster folding lock is very well designed.  As you fold it up the sectional lock links click into place and a silicon band secures the rest.  The result is a silent lock when you are riding, and it also comes with a belt clip so that you don't have to attach anything to the bike.  This is my second folding lock, I also have the Abus, a well-known brand that I have been using for about 5 years.  It is an excellent lock, but the Foldy has improved on that design.  The Foldy is considerably heavier, maybe half as much again, and I thought it would drag my belt and pants down but that didn't happen.  The Foldy is very quiet, something I am particular about.  The Abus comes in a plastic box that you velcro to the frame and it rattles around abominably in there so I threw the case away and began to secure the Abus with a length of velcro to quieten it down.  The Clipster has designed that modification in, while also securing the linkages and adding the belt clip.  In terms of diameter, both locks are the same, so you won't be hitching up to a thick pole, but any skinny street sign or bike rack will be fine.  The price point for both locks is the same.  3 keys provided.

Marinex Glass Custard Cup, 8-1/2-Ounce This 8-1/2 ounce MARINEX GLASS CUSTARD CUP is slightly larger than the small Pyrex custard cups that I've always used for baked custard. However, it's still a very convenient size for single servings of custard, pudding, or ice cream.

The Marinex brand is expensive, but superior to the present-day Pyrex brand, because Marinex glass cookware is made from borosilicate glass. Borosilicate glass, which has a slight green tinge, is less susceptible to thermal shock than the tempered soda lime glass used by Pyrex. (Years ago, Pyrex dishes were also made of borosilicate glass.) I feel safer using glass cookware made with borosilicate glass, because some of my newer Pyrex dishes have shattered when they were removed from the oven and placed on a room-temperature, ceramic-tile countertop. (Now I always place glass cookware on a hotpad or oven mitt.)

When I ordered this item, I thought that the listing must be for four Marinex custard cups, because of the price (about $16). In fact, I received just one custard cup, as the listing promises. The single custard cup is a genuine Marinex custard cup, and it is identical to the ones in the four-cup set that I purchased from Amazon for about the same price (see [[ASIN:B008H07AQC Marinex Set of Four Glass Custard Cups, 8-1/2-Ounce]]). Because this is a 5-star product with a 1-star price, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

text_fidelity_a:
GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing I selected this luminous key ring as an aid to attaching to my camera bag and being visible at night. I wasn’t exactly sure what to expect and I had some serious doubts about the effectiveness of this product. It turns out that it’s better than I had hoped and it works well.

The concept is very simple: expose it to bright light for a little while and it will glow in the dark for a longer while. The claim is that it will glow for up to 10 hours; I have not verified that it will last that long, but it does go for a long time, long enough in most situations that it will continue to glow long after sunset. This is really all I can ask.

The vial appears to be filled with some sort of phosphorous-coated granules. As a first test I exposed them to the bright light of an LED flashlight for about 30 seconds, and the vial glowed for several minutes afterward. It wasn’t all that bright, but I didn’t give it long to “charge” either. It was enough as a proof of concept though. It lasts longer under extended exposure to bright light such as direct sunlight.

The extra clips that come with the vial are useful for attaching it to other things without using the ring. One of the attachments is actually the same thing as a pen clip, which is useful for clipping to a tent flap, umbrella or other fabric surface.

Especially when considering the cost, this is really an easy product to recommend if you need a luminous marker. It really does work for a long while, it’s very easy to see and it is versatile.
text_fidelity_b: GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail Where I live it is important to have back up food sources. Sometimes we get severe weather and that can mean an inability to go to the grocery store, no electricity, or sometimes snowed in for a while. I always try to have some different foods on hand that are easy to fix for such times as that, but one thing I have not had is vegetables for long term storage, should we have to go through an extended time of roughing it.

WHAT IS THIS COLLECTION LIKE?
WHAT SIZE BUCKET?
First of all, it comes in a four gallon sized bucket which is square. That means it will fit on the shelf more easily and be easier to stack. This baby was SEALED tight. It has a tab that you pull which starts a plastic strip coming off from around the entire rim of the bucket. The size is 13 1/2 inches high and 10 inches square.

HOW WAS THIS BUCKET TO OPEN?
I have to say that this bucket was VERY difficult to open. If you are older, or have a weak grip, this might be very difficult to open- especially in an emergency. Of course, being hungry might motivate you enough to push through, but honestly, I am pretty strong and this particular bucket was so hard to open I had to get pliers and then pull with all of my might many times to work it off of the bucket.

WHAT IS THE BUCKET LIKE INSIDE?
Inside the rim is a rubberized seal. I would assume that the way this was sealed that it would withstand reasonable water around it- perhaps not for a really long time, but enough to keep the contents dry for a bit should you need to be in the rain or have a flood in your storage area. There is a little crunched up bunch of powder inside which I am thinking was at one time a moisture control tab, but I can not say for sure.

There is a bit more space in the bucket so that you could keep other freeze dried pouches in here, or perhaps plastic dishes or other things you want to put in with it for saving space, such as vacuum sealed spices, or other mixes you might have accumulated or made. It is important that they are sealed, however as you don't want to have bugs get into the bucket over time from just loosely bagged foods. Also I would avoid grains in a bucket like this as they can still hatch bugs which will eat through vacuum sealed bags- ask me how I know..

WHAT IS IN THE BUCKET?
This is where I was a bit disappointed. The outside clearly lists what is in the bucket, but for the price, I expected to have a little better quality than this. There are metallic bags in this bucket most of which are vacuum sealed. Two of them are not, however. One of them is onions, but the other was not even labeled. It turned out to be potatoes, but there was not anything on the bag at all to indicate that it was potatoes. I would have thought that it would be labeled and vacuum sealed for the onions and potatoes. Perhaps there is a reason why they are not.

HOW PRACTICAL IS THIS KIT?
This kit has 109 servings in it. That is a lot, but the problem is that each package of vegetables is the entire contents of the bucket. For instance, it might have 15 servings of peas in one pouch, but let's say you do not want to have peas all of the time. Perhaps you have a quick emergency for a few days and then it is over. The problem is that once you open the bag of peas, the shelf life goes down quickly.

So, once you open a bag, you have to finish it in a reasonable amount of time and keep ti sealed in a jar perhaps for longer storage. It will NOT last 20 years as advertised however once opened.

HOW IS THIS KIT BEST USED?
This kit is best used as a 1 week supply for food. A few weeks at best. That means if you buy this kit, then you will have to plan on using what is inside all at once- at least each vegetable that you open. That means you should buy multiple packs if you want to have a long term storage that you can rely on over an extended period.

DRAWBACKS
I would have liked to see the pouches broken down in thirds or even halves. That way if you open one, you still have another for future use, up to 20 years. I also was not sure why the potatoes and onions were not vacuum sealed and why the potatoes are not labeled. They are a part of the kit, so they should have been labeled like the rest of the bags in the bucket.

QUALITY
The vegetables tasted good- they are freeze dried which means that you can eat them as a crunchy snack food without breaking your teeth as you would with dehydrated food. You can also cook with them, but honestly they were so good as snacks that is how we enjoyed them. It is important that you drink plenty of water when eating freeze dried foods, however. We would always have them right out of the bag at our house which is the best way to have the most nutrients.

I love that this has no added sugar or other ingredients like most "survival" food does. It is just vegetables and that fits our family perfectly as we do not eat sugar or highly processed foods.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although the bucket is very difficult to get into (at least this one was), the food inside is well protected from weather and elements. The food is sealed in large bags of each type, so you need to use up what you open in a reasonable amount of time. Not all of the bags were vacuum sealed and one was not marked, so I give this four stars for that.

As for the purchase and having it handy, it is an excellent kit to have on hand, especially if you live in an area that is prone to severe weather. I would reiterate that it would be best to have a collection of these handy as this one will only feed a small family for a short period of time.

I will update with more information should I have anything else to report in the future.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail

My only reservation is the spacing. I measured slightly under 113mm on the old spindle, so figured the 113mm UN55 would be the tiniest bit wide. In fact it was a tiny bit narrow, as the chainrings lined up slightly to the left of where they were. I adjusted the limit screw and tension on the front derailleur and the bike seems to work fine now. Not sure whether I should try a wider BB or what; I'm new to proper road bike mechanics. Also I didn't actually measure the new spindle to verify that it really is 113mm; I only noticed the discrepancy after I assembled the whole thing and I didn't want to back out all the parts just to measure....

Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M I bought this from Amazon based on all the 5 star reviews. I have been wearing it consistently for 11 days and following the instructions as noted in the on-line user guide videos. I am torn as to whether to give this 3 or 4 start. I ended up going with 4 stars because I have tried other trackers and the REIGN feature-set is hands above the other devices I have tried. For me it is the best choice available, today.

PROS
SIZING: Band design and fit is excellent. You are given 3 band lengths with every device, which ensure you will get the perfect custom fit. Before you buy, I strongly recommend you go the the Jaybird REIGN site's FAQ pg for exact sizing info. http://www.jaybirdsport.com/static/img/reign/sizing-guide.jpg
Be aware, you want to determine the side-to-side width across the TOP of your wrist, not the circumference of your wrist. The REIGN is a 2 piece band. The fit/width of the top piece is what determines which size to buy. You then customize your fit with the bottom band, which is provided in 3 lengths.

SECURE: the magnetic locking mechanism ensures your band will never fall off. The design allows you to easily secure your band with one hand. Once it is magnetically secured, it will not come off until you manually disengage the magnets. Excellent design!

COMFORT: Due to the lightweight, smooth silicone band, this is the MOST comfortable activity wearable I have ever tried. As a tech professional, I am typing on my keyboard all day long and cannot wear any watch-type devices or jewelry on my wrists. This is the 1st tracker device I have found that I can wear all day, every day. I barely notice it's on my wrist. I wipe mine down with a damp cloth. I have had no irritation or discomfort. 5 stars!

TRACKING: The REIGN will track data by specific activity, which you will not get with other devices. It detects Walking, Swimming, Biking, Running and General activity. In addition to the 3 silicone magnetic wrist bands, they provide 2 stretch style athletic bands and an ankle biking band. The STEP tracking is accurate for me ( Compared my data for a couple of days with a FitBit and Treadmill)

SMART PHONE APP: The design of the SmartPhone app is a plus. The information provided is very good. In additional to your GoZone score, you are given 3 screens of data: Activity, Sleep and History. Each screen presents you with a Summary view and a Detail 'Timeline' view of that data.

VISUAL FEEDBACK: The band itself provides visual indication of your progress towards your GoZone Goal via lights. Each light represents 9% of your goal. (Dont bother enabling the 'Time' feature. The lights flash for 1 second and is pretty much useless)

CHARGING: Very easy to pop the device out of the band and charge on the charger that is included. Via USB cord, it can be charged thru your laptop or a plug, your choice. As stated, it takes about 3 hrs to initially charge. I pop mine onto the charger before I hop in the shower. Easy-peasy. Please note, if you lose the charger, you will have to buy a replacement since the charging doc is required.

USER GUIDE: I recommend you watch the online User Guide videos AND read thru the entire list of FAQs prior to purchasing/using the REIGN. There is a lot of info in the FAQs that is not covered in the User Guide videos that you will want to be aware of. A nice feature is, the videos are also part of the SmartPhone app.

HISTORY: the SmartPhone app. provides a History screen with Day, Week, Month & Year mode. Once you select your mode, you can then swipe thru by Day, Week, Month...... Very nice.

PERSONALIZED: The REIGN definitely does 'get to know you'. After the 1st week or so, the daily goal has adjusted, based on my history.

CONS:
GO ZONE: Upon waking up, you should be able to sync and log that day's GO ZONE feedback in 2 minutes. I have owned the REIGN for 11 days and rarely have I been ale to get GO ZONE to completed on the 1st try. Once the REIGN device is Connected to the SmartPhone app. and I Start Go Zone, I often get error messages and have to Start again. These issues are definitely specific to the GO ZONE feature, as I do not get errors throughout the day when syncing. This is the key feature of the device, so I expect it to work without issue and not have to battle with it.

SUPPORT: Unfortunately, I cannot give a good review on support. I sent a very detailed Email with screenshots from my SmartPhone listing the GoZone errors and Sleep monitoring issue I have experienced. The response I received was very friendly, however the only thing the reply told me was I could manually enter Sleep info in the app. There was no response to my detailed GoZone issues and questions.
SUPPORT Review Update 12-29-2015: I received another reply from Jaybird Support addressing my specific concerns and questions. They have provided me with instructions of how to reset my Reign pod, indicating this may resolve my specific issues.

READABILITY: I think the design of the app is great and it is easy to use. However, it is not so easy to read on your Smart Phone due to the funky color of the font (pale yellow-green) against a light grey background. It is not configurable. I understand these are the branded colors, but they do not lend themselves to readability on mobile devices.

DASHBOARD: There is not an online Dashboard. Your data is only available via your SmartPhone app. I went to the website and attempted to login assuming there would be an online dashboard. The online login is a separate account and is for purchases, only. The other tracker devices I have used have online Dashboards and settings, which I deem as a plus.

DATA SYNC: Data sync is on-demand, which preserves you SmartPhone battery (Yay!). However, for some reason, data for previous day(s) is not always shown in the app. Periodically, when you open the app on your phone, it will show all zero's after syncing. I have not been able to detect a pattern. It is an intermittent issue that cannot be reproduced, on demand. The work-a-round is to close and reopen the app.

TACTILE: Tapping the REIGN device 4 times does not active my lights. I have to rap it pretty hard, 8 to 12 times. I have mine set for progress feedback, only. The lights flash for 1 second. I would prefer a button that will allow me to quickly turn on the progress lights and turn them off when I release the button. ( If there were a manual button, the 'Time' feature may be of value).
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M

You will need a backpack or someway of carrying this reservoir since it does not have straps or anyway to attach to your body like it is. 1-23-21 okay I should have got back to this sooner everything in the first part of my review stands . text_fidelity_a:
SCHWINN Fitness 230 Recumbent Bike Wow! This bike has all the bells and whistles and is comfortable, too! While recumbent bikes aren't as good an overall workout as elliptical machines or upright bikes (since you're sitting), they are still low-impact and can help with the lower half of the body, as well as provide some cardio.

I'll go item by item, since there are so many noteworthy features:

**Ease of Assembly: 5 stars
The manual covered everything, and while it took some time to put together, everything went smoothly and came out perfectly. Not difficult, and it took well under two hours. I am female and assembled it with no help, so don't worry about anything being too heavy...as long as you don't try moving the box. (The delivery guys were more than happy to bring the box inside, earning them an unsolicited tip, but if that's not the case for you, just open the box and bring the parts in individually. No big deal.)

**Features and Settings: 5 stars
You can enter user data with age, height, and gender, to get better and more accurate results. Combined with sensors that let you see your heart rate, you can see what sort of activity you are doing (cardiovascular, fat burning, etc.), and unlike with some other machines, the heart rate sensor worked fine. Other features included different pre-programmed settings like workouts with alternating difficulties in patterns set to any time or level you like.

**Extras: 5 stars
There is a USB port to charge your mobile or tablet device!! You can also plug into the auxiliary port to use the speakers and play music--it even comes with the cable needed! The speakers are pretty loud and clear for something like this, so it's a great add-on! There is also a three-setting fan that works well when you get hot.

**Overall workout: 5 stars
The smooth movement and comfortable seating with air holes to allow your skin to breathe, along with so many extra features, make this an excellent workout tool, with the quality you would expect from a good gym. I LOVE this machine!
text_fidelity_b: SCHWINN Fitness 230 Recumbent Bike

This is an olive green hat with a small brim, a chin cord, and a ponytail hole. I’m specifying since there are a few different Jeff & Aimy hats under this listing.

I spend a lot of time outside during the warm months. I usually wear a baseball hat and headphones because I use a lot of noisy equipment, but I wanted a hat with a brim for when I’m pulling weeds or the like. I especially liked the mention of a ponytail hole, since my hair is rapidly reaching Rapunzel levels under quarantine.

Unfortunately, this hat is too big for me. It kept sliding around on my head and then falling over my eyes. I had to keep stopping whatever I was doing and adjust it, which got old pretty quick. I ended up taking the hat off less than ten minutes after putting it on and going back to my old standby baseball hat.

I would say the hat runs large, so if you are petite or usually adjust baseball caps to the smallest size, this might not be a good hat for you.

The brim is not very wide, nor does it provide good protection for the back of the neck. The brim swoops up in the back where the ponytail hole is, so it leaves the back of my neck bare.

The hat is made in China from 97% cotton and 3% spandex. The mesh is 100% polyester.

text_fidelity_a:
Swiss Cargo SCKJ02Q02 3 in 1 Kayak Carrier, Black I just got these (5/27/18) so I will be coming back to edit after next weekend when I use these for a two hour drive on the freeway, but for now I wanted to leave a review because of the 'screws not lining up' that I'm seeing on so many reviews.

I bought mine at Dunham's, which are already "seconds" so if anything I'd expect things like screws not quite lining up, but I think those reviewers just made the same assumption I did at first: that you install the two screws through the middle holes in the flat rubber bottom. That is incorrect!! The screws actually go in diagonal holes to form half of an X. I found that it really created a nice grip and being on a diagonal meant the maximum surface area possible of the attachy bit hugging my crossbars. So just an FYI - I wouldn't put a lot of stock in the "holes not lining up" reviews. One glance at the directions shows you how to properly attach the screws at opposite corners. Also note that the teeth on the middle bar may not tightly lock together right out of the box. Mine didn't. But then I realized that the red thing that locks them down also rotates to loosen or tighten those teeth together so now everything is good and locked.

EDIT: I'm back to give my review - I actually returned these. Problems I found: 1. the bottom of the J is flat instead of in the actual J shape. Seems like that would make it easier to load but it doesn't because if you put it in the center of your roof to use with two kayaks it is pretty far from the edge of your roof so lifting the kayak into the holder becomes difficult just due to how much roof you have to clear before you reach the rack, and sliding the kayak on from the rear doesn't work either because of the flat instead of actual J design, so there is nothing holding your kayak onto the device when you slide it up onto the roof and it just falls over the side of the car. You need someone else to at least spot the kayak to make sure it doesn't fall so this carrier requires two people.

The second issue is that it is very small. If you have two little 8 footers it should be fine but if you have an Old Towne or a Wilderness or really any brand of fishing kayak you are only going to be able to fit one in this holder because without that J shape you have to lean the center bracket way back to hold your wider kayak without it plunging back to the ground before you can ever get it fastened up.

The one thing I liked was the way it attached to the cross bars. That diagonal design AND the way they designed it so one side has a typical screw hole but the other side is a non-closed hole so you can screw on both bolts and then swing the underneath 'arm' onto the second bolt and tighten to your crossbars, makes it easier than trying to start the screw/bolt from completely unattached while on a roof of a car. It's hard to explain without seeing it, but you'll have to take my word that it's a nice feature the makers obviously considered when designing the product.

It did hold my kayak securely (with the center bar at about 145 degrees), I just didn't see a point in keeping a holder for two kayaks when it would only hold one of my kayak's size. I used these on ROLA aftermarket crossbars, aero shaped 3.5", found here on Amazon and it fit very well on those bars. Construction I would say is excellent.
text_fidelity_b: Swiss Cargo SCKJ02Q02 3 in 1 Kayak Carrier, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Hydraform Reservoir Cleaning Kit I'm pretty frusted with this cleaning kit. Previously I've used CamelBak reservoirs and their cleaning it so everything is in comparison.

For Osprey, opening is slightly smaller which means I cannot fit my hand inside reservoir to scrub inside of it. The brush fits but you really can't get any elbow grease going with it.

For both Osprey and Camel - the dang flexible tube brush is SHORTER than the tube. I just don't get this. It's 5-10 inches too short. Either sell a brush slight longer than half the length, forcing users to go in from both ends. Or, sell a brush slightly longer than the whole thing.So it can be cleaned completely in one fell swoop. Instead of forcing me to use an awkwardly long brush that still needs to be stuck in from both ends.

For Osprey - it is MUCH harder to detaching drinking tube from reservoir so this discourages proper cleaning and too short brush leaves 5 or so inches of disgusting goo left in drinking tube.

For Osprey - the drying rack thing really doesn't fit in reservoir. I forced it in during first use and then really, really struggled to get it back out. Now I only stick it in 3/4 of the way - because at least I can get it back out that way. The plastic is super cheap and every time I bend it it looks very fragile. I can imagine this lasting in real world camping conditions where its going to be exposed to extreme heat and UV light. Mine lives in my kitchen so doing ok so far. CamelPak's 'wings' design is far superior.

Mesh bag it comes in. Pretty snazzy but so form fitting no one is going to use this again to hold the cleaning kit because it is such a tight fit - could be used as a stuff sack for something else - maybe eating ware??

So overall - just awkward to use because there were a million ways to better design this especially when CamelPak is just sitting there with obvious design improvements. But still, mostly it works and is better than trying to use non-custom brushes for same purpose.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Hydraform Reservoir Cleaning Kit

text_fidelity_a:
GLIDING DISCS ULTIMATE BUNS AND LEGS WORKOUT AS SEEN ON TV I have done gliding-type moves in other workouts and enjoyed them, so I was eager to try this set. The term Gliding is trademarked by fitness instructor Mindy Mylrea, and this is the original set of 3 workouts on one disk sold via infomercial. The workouts including Ultimate Buns and Legs, Fat Burning Cardio, and Total Body Workout. This set also includes two gliding discs designed for use on carpet (discs for use on smooth flooring are sold elsewhere).

The Ultimate Buns & Legs workout is an approximately 35-minute workout focused on the lower body. It begins with a 6-minute warm-up which includes shoulder rolls, squats (moving side-to-side with discs under the feet), and stretches. About 10 minutes of standing leg work follows: you will do single leg squats, first to either side, then to the rear, and then move into double leg squats. This segment includes a 2-minute stretch before moving to the floor. The floor work includes bridge moves (with the discs under your heels), side and plank work, and finally, some brief back extensions for a total of about 15 minutes. The workout ends with a 4-minute seated stretch which includes twists. Overall, I liked this workout; I felt that it gave me a bit of a cardio effect, and I felt a slight soreness in the backs of my legs the next day.

Fat Burning Cardio is a 37-minute aerobic interval workout which alternates 4-6 minute cardio intervals with 3-minute toning segments using the discs. The workout begins with a 6.5 minute warm-up which includes side steps, hamstring curls, and knee lifts; the warm-up ends with squats and lunges using the discs. The first cardio interval is about 4 minutes and includes marches with a V-step, eventually adding on mambos and small hops (I recognized music from Firm videos here). The first toning segment consists of squats and single leg lunges; the lunges are performed both to the side and to the back, moving from a slow to fast tempo. The next cardio segment is a little longer at about 6 minutes, and it includes side steps with a direction change, adding jumping jacks, lunges with a hop, and heel digs with a hop; my calves were really burning during this segment! In the toning segment which follows, you will do circle lunges (using the disc around one foot and making a circle around the other disk), and slow side squats remaining in a crouched position. The final cardio interval is 5 minutes long and starts with a chasse/lunge combo, adding scoops and jogs. The last gliding segment has more side squats as well as a back-side-back lunge combination. This workout finishes with a 5-minute stretch which targets the hamstrings, thighs, and hip flexors. Again, I felt some soreness from this workout the next day (mainly in my calves), but I was a bit disappointed that my heart rate was only in my target zone for less than 20 minutes.

The final workout in this set is the Total Body Workout, a 54-minute workout targeting the entire body. The 6.5-minute warm-up is similar to the ones above, featuring side steps with shoulder rolls and squats using the disks. The next part of the workout is 29.5 minutes of standing leg work. Again, the moves are similar to those done in the above two workouts--eg, squats, single leg lunges, circle lunges, etc.--but for some reason, I enjoyed them more here. A brief standing stretch follows before moving on to the floor work, which begins with an additional 2-minute stretch in a seated position. Next comes 5 minutes of abs work on your back, using the discs both under the heels and under the hands. Following this comes 5 minutes of side-lying work, about 7 minutes of bride and very tough plank work (again using the disks both under the hands and under the feet), and finally, a 4-minute floor stretch. I particularly enjoyed the standing portion of this workout (which actually put me in my target HR zone for over 20 minutes), and I felt more soreness in my legs the next day than I did with the Ultimate Buns & Legs workout.

Overall, I liked these workouts a lot, and I think getting them together on one DVD is a great deal. I find gliding to be a lot of fun, and use of the discs definitely seems to work my muscles in unique ways (for example, I felt my inner thighs working much more than usual). I would definitely recommend this set, and I give it a rating of 4 1/2 stars.
text_fidelity_b: GLIDING DISCS ULTIMATE BUNS AND LEGS WORKOUT AS SEEN ON TV

text_fidelity_a: VIPERTEK VTS-881 - 39 Billion Micro Stun Gun - Rechargeable with LED Flashlight, Green I don't have an exciting or dramatic tale of self-defense to share, but I actually did use a Vipertek taser to protect myself once. He was barking aggressively and advancing little by little. I first yelled as loud as I could for the neighbors to come get their dog, but there was no response. I have made a habit of carrying a taser, and I had a Vipertek flashlight style one in my pocket. The dog was still barking and gradually advancing on me. I didn't dare turn my back to it. I drew out the taser, turned it on, and hit the zap button. BRRZZZAPPP! went the noise. The dog immediately stopped barking -- not another sound -- and ran back home. I never noticed him barking at me again. So just the noise did the trick. I decided to downsize to this smaller, more pocketable version. I carry it in a cell phone bag.
